headline: A December 2022 law keeps the federal government funded at 2022 levels through December 30, 2022, and extends several expiring programs.
what_it_does: Division A is a continuing resolution, which lets federal agencies keep operating at fiscal year 2022 funding levels while Congress finishes the 2023 spending bills. Without it, a government shutdown would have started when the prior funding expired on December 23, 2022. Division B extends several programs and authorities through December 30, 2022, including FCC spectrum auctions, a special assessment that funds human-trafficking survivor programs, the U.S. Parole Commission, a Commodity Futures Trading Commission fund account, and limits on Indian Health Service payments to certain Alaska Native entities. A separate title exempts the budget effects of the law from certain pay-as-you-go and scorekeeping rules.

who_it_affects.group: federal employees and federal agency workers
who_it_affects.how: Their agencies keep receiving funding so they can continue operating without a shutdown.

who_it_affects.group: people who receive services from federal agencies
who_it_affects.how: Federal programs continue running at 2022 funding levels instead of stopping when the prior funding ran out.

who_it_affects.group: people and organizations convicted of certain sexual abuse or human trafficking offenses
who_it_affects.how: A special assessment that applies to them is extended, and the money goes to programs for human-trafficking survivors.

who_it_affects.group: Alaska Native villages and corporations in areas served by Alaska Native regional health entities
who_it_affects.how: Limits on Indian Health Service disbursing funds to them are extended.

who_it_affects.group: companies that bid on FCC electromagnetic spectrum licenses
who_it_affects.how: The FCC's authority to hold spectrum license auctions is extended.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted December 23, 2022; the funding and extensions run through December 30, 2022, or until the applicable FY2023 appropriations act is enacted, whichever is earlier.
